body:
You are a dialogue and narration writer for a single-player dark-fantasy RPG based on Curse of Strahd, set in the gloomy, mist-bound valley of Barovia. Reply with plain text only (no JSON, no markdown, no code fences, no preamble, no commentary after) and do not send messages to any other agent. Write only what is asked, in the exact format asked.

SETTING OF THIS TASK: the catacombs under Castle Ravenloft, where the old house of von Zarovich buries its dead in rows of iron-gated crypts, each with a name over the gate. The party is level 10. Count Strahd von Zarovich is the vampire lord of the castle. The crypts are orderly, cold and almost tender; the horror is how long everything has waited. A few of the book's crypts are comic (a chef with a bell, a knight who tripped on his own sword, a rich man's painted gold coins). Those keep their joke deadpan and never wink at the player.

TONE: gothic horror with dry, understated, character-driven humour. Funny comes from specifics and deadpan, not from jokes about the horror. Where a scene is sad, let it be sad. No modern slang, no pop culture, no real-world references. Do not invent other named people than the ones given. Do not use em-dashes (use commas, colons or full stops). Do not use semicolons more than once in a line. Plain words a voice actor can read aloud.

NARRATOR STYLE (second person, present tense, one or two sentences). Samples from the existing game, to match voice, length and rhythm:
- A bronze plaque, green with age: the old king's champion, who never lost a fight. It lists the men he killed. It takes up the whole plaque.
- Over the foot of the stair, two words cut deep and plain: HE RESTS. Nothing about peace.
- The lord of the house in marble, seated, a wolf at his feet. The sculptor made him kinder than he is, and the stone has not forgiven either of them.
- Words are cut over the stair: the house keeps its dead. Someone has added, below it, in a smaller hand: and its dead keep the house.
Carved words are written in CAPITALS inside the sentence, as in the samples.

TASK: write spoken lines for four short conversations in the crypts. Output format, one per line, nothing else:
LINE_ID: the line
Speech lines are at most 36 words, in the speaker's own voice, first person. "Option" lines are what the player's party says to choose that branch: at most 10 words, a plain question or statement. A "Narrator" line follows the narrator style above (second person, present tense, at most 32 words). Never repeat a joke or sentence shape between lines. No speaker ever winks at the player; the comedy is in their certainty and their details.

WHAT THE PLAYER KNOWS (use as the facts the skulls speak about):
- Count Strahd sleeps by day in a plain wooden coffin in his tomb at the bottom of the black stair, under the hall of names in these catacombs.
- He cannot be ended for good until he has been beaten once. Beaten anywhere, he dissolves into mist and flees to that coffin. Then he can be finished there with a wooden stake, the sunlight of the sword called the Sunsword, or the Holy Symbol of Ravenkind.
- In the old range of crypts called the Lesser Vaults, the crypt of Saint Finderway has two alcoves. One of them carries a traveller, instantly, into the alcoves of the count's own tomb, and the other brings them back.

CONVERSATION 1: THE SKULL OF STEFAN GREGOROVICH, counsellor to King Barov, on a shelf in his crypt. A magic skull. It answers any question with total confidence and is ALWAYS wrong; every answer must be false in a way the player can tell is false. Pompous, formal, a courtier who was never contradicted. He never admits he is wrong.
STEFAN_GREET: his greeting when the party stands before him.
STEFAN_OPT_SLEEP: option: ask where the count sleeps.
STEFAN_SLEEP: his wrong answer (not the real place).
STEFAN_OPT_END: option: ask how the count is ended for good.
STEFAN_END: his wrong answer (something absurdly gentle or useless).
STEFAN_OPT_ALCOVES: option: ask what the alcoves in Saint Finderway's crypt do.
STEFAN_ALCOVES: his wrong answer (something harmless and wrong).
STEFAN_OPT_LEAVE: option: leave him be.
STEFAN_BYE: his farewell, certain that the party will thank him.

CONVERSATION 2: THE SKULL OF INTREE SIK-VALOO, a scholar from a far country, on a shelf in his crypt. A magic skull. He answers any question with total accuracy. Quiet, exact, a little weary, slightly amused that anyone still asks. He knows that the skull of Stefan Gregorovich, two crypts away, always lies, and finds it faintly embarrassing.
INTREE_GREET: his greeting when the party stands before him; he says he answers truly, and warns that Stefan's skull in the next crypt does not.
INTREE_OPT_SLEEP: option: ask where the count sleeps.
INTREE_SLEEP: his true answer, from the facts above.
INTREE_OPT_END: option: ask how the count is ended for good.
INTREE_END: his true answer, from the facts above.
INTREE_OPT_ALCOVES: option: ask what the alcoves in Saint Finderway's crypt do.
INTREE_ALCOVES: his true answer, with a plain warning that on the other side lies the count's own tomb.
INTREE_OPT_LEAVE: option: leave him be.
INTREE_BYE: his farewell.

CONVERSATION 3: SASHA IVLISKOVA, a vampire spawn "wife", bound in thick grey webs on her bier in a crypt of the Lesser Vaults. When the party speaks to her she wakes. Sweet, hopeful and lonely at first, then venomous when disappointed. She has been waiting for her husband, Ivan Ivliskovich the champion dog-racer, for far longer than she knows.
SASHA_WAKE: her first words as she wakes: she asks if her love has come for her.
SASHA_OPT_WHO: option: ask who she is waiting for.
SASHA_WHO: her answer about Ivan and the racing hounds; wistful and a little proud.
SASHA_OPT_NO: option: tell her the truth, that no one is coming.
SASHA_NO: her reaction, turning from tender to deadly in one breath; the fight starts after it.
SASHA_OPT_LEAVE: option: ease the lid shut and leave her sleeping.
SASHA_LEAVE: a Narrator line: the party lowers the lid and the webs settle; faint relief and a hint of a sob.

CONVERSATION 4: SIR KLUTZ TRIPALOTSKY, the ghost of a knight who tripped and fell on his own sword. When the party pulls the sword out of his skeleton's breastplate, his ghost steps out of the stone. Cheerful, eager, courteous and terribly clumsy; he apologises for things that have not happened yet. He offers to help the party in one fight, once, and then must rest.
KLUTZ_APPEARS: a Narrator line: his ghost steps from the stone, tall and gleaming, and promptly catches a boot on the threshold.
KLUTZ_OFFER: his thanks, and his offer to fight beside the party for one battle.
KLUTZ_OPT_JOIN: option: accept his help.
KLUTZ_JOIN: his delighted acceptance.
KLUTZ_OPT_REST: option: decline and tell him to rest.
KLUTZ_REST: his gracious, slightly crestfallen farewell as he lies back down.
KLUTZ_OPT_SWORD: option: say you will put the sword back.
KLUTZ_SWORD: his reaction (he is perfectly fine about it, and says something about how it went in).
result:
STEFAN_GREET: Stand straight when you address the royal council. I am Stefan Gregorovich, first adviser to King Barov, and you have my leave to ask whatever small question troubles you.
STEFAN_OPT_SLEEP: Where does Count Strahd sleep?
STEFAN_SLEEP: In the high bell tower, naturally, suspended in a hammock of woven silver thread where the morning sun may warm his boots.
STEFAN_OPT_END: How is the count ended for good?
STEFAN_END: Present him with a bowl of salted plum broth and three polite knocks upon his shield. No gentleman of the blood can withstand proper courtly notice.
STEFAN_OPT_ALCOVES: What do the alcoves in Saint Finderway's crypt do?
STEFAN_ALCOVES: They are airing cupboards for the castle linen. Step into the left one if you wish your cloak pressed and lightly scented with lavender.
STEFAN_OPT_LEAVE: We will leave you to your thoughts.
STEFAN_BYE: Do not trouble yourselves with formal thanks. Mention my counsel to the chamberlain as you go, and mind your posture on the stairs.
INTREE_GREET: You have come a long way to ask questions of bone. Ask, and I will answer truly, which cannot be said for poor Stefan Gregorovich two doors down.
INTREE_OPT_SLEEP: Where does the count sleep?
INTREE_SLEEP: By day he lies in a plain wooden coffin in his tomb at the foot of the black stair, beneath the hall of names.
INTREE_OPT_END: How can the count be ended for good?
INTREE_END: Beat him once so he flees as mist to his coffin. Finish him there with a wooden stake, the Sunsword's sunlight, or the Holy Symbol of Ravenkind.
INTREE_OPT_ALCOVES: What do the alcoves in Saint Finderway's crypt do?
INTREE_ALCOVES: One carries you in an instant to the alcoves inside the count's own tomb, and the other brings you back. Step only if you mean to meet him.
INTREE_OPT_LEAVE: Thank you. We will let you rest.
INTREE_BYE: Go carefully. The stone here remembers footsteps longer than it remembers names.
SASHA_WAKE: Is that your lantern at the gate, my heart? Have you come down at last to fetch me home?
SASHA_OPT_WHO: Who is it you are waiting for?
SASHA_WHO: My husband, Ivan Ivliskovich. His greyhounds took the winter riband three years running, and he promised we should have a house by the river when the snow melted.
SASHA_OPT_NO: No one is coming for you.
SASHA_NO: You lie with a warm throat. If Ivan is not behind you, then you have only brought me supper.
SASHA_OPT_LEAVE: Ease the stone lid back into place.
SASHA_LEAVE: You lower the stone into its groove and the grey webs settle back across her face. From the dark beneath comes a small breath of relief, and one dry sob.
KLUTZ_APPEARS: A tall ghost in bright mail steps out of the stone, bows with great dignity, and catches his left spur squarely on the threshold.
KLUTZ_OFFER: My earnest thanks for the iron, friends, and my apologies in advance if I tread upon your cloaks. I have one good battle left in me, if you will have me.
KLUTZ_OPT_JOIN: Come with us. We would be glad of your sword.
KLUTZ_JOIN: Splendid! Lead on, and pray stand a pace to my right, as my scabbard has a wicked habit of swinging when I turn.
KLUTZ_OPT_REST: Your wars are done, sir. Rest now.
KLUTZ_REST: Ah. Quite right, of course; a wise captain keeps his ranks tidy. I shall just lie back down here and try not to rattle.
KLUTZ_OPT_SWORD: We should put the sword back where it was.
KLUTZ_SWORD: Oh, do not mind on my account. It went in between the fourth and fifth ribs when my heel met the stair, and truthfully, I had grown used to the draught.
